This whole song is four chords, played over and over: **G, D, Em, C**. Many hit songs are built on
this loop. Everyone in the class plays the same song at the same time. Each player picks a level.

- **Level 1** is for your first day on the instrument.
- **Level 4** is for players who already play.
- Start at the level you can play **without stopping**. Move up when you can play it through four
  times without looking at your hands.

**How to use the page.** Press **▶ Play** and the band plays the loop. Under **Who plays**, switch
your own instrument off and play its part yourself. The buttons under each example pick the
level. The band plays exactly the part you choose, and it is written out underneath. Use the
tempo control at the bottom of the window to slow it down.

**Count it.** Every chord lasts one bar: four beats. Count "1, 2, 3, 4" out loud. The chord
changes on every "1".

| Bar | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Chord | G | D | Em | C |
| Bass note | G | D | E | C |

## Drums

You play with both feet and both hands. The **bass drum** (right foot) and the **snare drum**
are the two most important sounds. The bass drum is low and goes on 1 and 3. The snare is
sharp and goes on 2 and 4. Together they make the **backbeat**, the beat under nearly all rock.

- **Level 1: Bass drum and snare.** Bass drum on 1 and 3, snare on 2 and 4. Just
  "boom, crack, boom, crack". (The band's drummer also taps the hi-hat pedal on 2 and 4. Skip
  that at first.)
- **Level 2: Add the hi-hat in quarter notes.** Your right hand plays the closed hi-hat on every
  beat. Your left hand plays the snare on 2 and 4. On 2 and 4, both hands hit at once.
- **Level 3: Hi-hat in eighth notes.** Count "1 and 2 and 3 and 4 and". The hi-hat plays on
  every number and every "and".
- **Level 4: The rock beat.** The bass drum moves around a little, and you play a fill at the
  end of each time through the loop. Next: [Hi-hat Grooves](hihat-grooves.qmd).

## Bass

The bass plays the lowest note of each chord. That note is the **root**, the letter name of
the chord: G, D, E, C. On a bass in standard tuning (E A D G, lowest string first):

| Chord | String | Fret |
|---|---|---|
| G | E (lowest) | 3 |
| D | A | 5 (or the open D string) |
| Em | E (lowest) | open |
| C | A | 3 |

- **Level 1: One note a bar.** Play the root on "1" and let it ring for four beats.
- **Level 2: Two notes a bar.** The root on 1 and on 3.
- **Level 3: Four notes a bar.** The root on every beat.
- **Level 4: Eighth notes.** The root eight times a bar: "1 and 2 and 3 and 4 and". This is
  the classic rock bass part. Lock in with the drummer's bass drum.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="G|D|Em|C" data-tempo="92" data-comp="guitar" data-on="bass comp drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Level:" data-choices='[{"label":"1: One note a bar","opts":{"bassFeel":"held","push":false}},{"label":"2: Root on 1 and 3","opts":{"bassFeel":"halves","push":false}},{"label":"3: Root on every beat","opts":{"bassFeel":"roots","push":false}},{"label":"4: Root eighths","opts":{"bassFeel":"eighths"}}]'></div>

## Guitar

There are two things to learn: the **chord shapes** (left hand) and the **strum** (right hand).
Pick a level of each. They do not have to match.

**Chord shapes.** Pick one row. The dots show where your fingers go; the number in each dot is
the note's place in the chord (1 = the root, 3, 5). An x above a string means don't play it.
Every shape opens in the [Chord Library](/tools/chord-library.html), with the other ways to play it.

*Easy shapes (one or two fingers).* The D is a D5: it has no F♯, but it fits the song.

<div class="sc-shapes" data-inst="guitar" data-shapes="G:xx0003 D5:xx023x Em:022000 C:xxx010"></div>

*Full open chords.* More on these in [Guitar Chord Shapes by Hand](chord-shapes-guitar-hand.qmd).

<div class="sc-shapes" data-inst="guitar" data-shapes="G:320003 D:xx0232 Em:022000 C:x32010"></div>

*Power chords* (for a louder, harder rock sound). Two fingers, the same shape every time; only
E5 uses an open string.

<div class="sc-shapes" data-inst="guitar" data-shapes="G5:35xxxx D5:x57xxx E5:02xxxx C5:x35xxx"></div>

**Strum.**

- **Level 1: One strum a bar.** Strum down on "1" and let it ring. This gives you three beats
  to get to the next chord.
- **Level 2: Down on every beat.** Four downstrokes a bar.
- **Level 3: Down, up.** Eight strums a bar: down on the numbers, up on the "and"s. Keep your
  arm moving even when you miss a string.
- **Level 4: D, D-U, D, D-U.** The folk-rock strum. Count "1, 2 and, 3, 4 and".

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="G|D|Em|C" data-tempo="92" data-comp="guitar" data-on="bass comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-choice-label="Level:" data-choices='[{"label":"1: One strum a bar","opts":{"compRhythm":"pad","push":false}},{"label":"2: Down on every beat","opts":{"compRhythm":"strumQuarters","push":false}},{"label":"3: Down-up eighths","opts":{"compRhythm":"strumEights","push":false}},{"label":"4: D, D-U, D, D-U","opts":{"compRhythm":"strumFolk"}}]'></div>

## Keyboard

The notes below stay close together, so your right hand barely moves.

Level 1 plays only the root, the note marked 1 (G, D, E, C). Level 2 and up play all three notes.

<div class="sc-shapes" data-inst="keyboard" data-shapes="G:55,59,62 D:57,62,66 Em:55,59,64 C:55,60,64"></div>

- **Level 1: One note a bar.** Play the root with your right thumb on "1" and hold it.
- **Level 2: The chord, once a bar.** Three notes together on "1", held for four beats.
- **Level 3: The chord on every beat**, with your left hand playing the root on "1".
- **Level 4: Driving eighths.** The chord eight times a bar, left hand on the root. Keep it
  light so that it does not cover the guitar.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="G|D|Em|C" data-tempo="92" data-comp="piano" data-on="bass comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-choice-label="Level:" data-choices='[{"label":"1 and 2: One chord a bar","opts":{"compRhythm":"pad","push":false}},{"label":"3: Chord on every beat","opts":{"compRhythm":"quarters","push":false}},{"label":"4: Driving eighths","opts":{"compRhythm":"eighths"}}]'></div>

## Voice, and instruments that play one note at a time

This is for singers, saxophone, violin, flute, trumpet and any other instrument that plays
one note at a time. (Saxophone and trumpet players: these are concert pitches. Ask which notes
to read on your instrument.)

- **Level 1: The roots.** Sing or play G, D, E, C, one long note a bar. This is the bass part
  sung higher.
- **Level 2: A smooth line.** B, A, B, C. Every note is in its chord, and each one is a step from
  the last. Sing it on "oo", then make up words.
- **Level 3: Make up a riff.** Use only the notes **G A B D E** (the G major pentatonic scale).
  They fit all four chords. Make a short rhythm, two beats long, and repeat it every bar.
- **Level 4: Make up a melody.** Use the same five notes. Play a short idea, then answer it
  with a different one, like a question and an answer. See also [Pop Singing](voice-pop.qmd).

Switch on all the players below and play along.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="G|D|Em|C" data-tempo="92" data-comp="guitar" data-on="bass comp drums" data-staves="bass"></div>

## The whole band

Everyone together. Turn off the players your class is covering. The buttons set every player
in the band to the same level, so you can hear what level 1 and level 4 sound like as a band.
They don't have to match: a level 1 bass under a level 4 drummer sounds fine.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="G|D|Em|C" data-tempo="92" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Band:" data-choices='[{"label":"Everyone at level 1","opts":{"groove":"boomchick","bassFeel":"held","compRhythm":"pad","push":false}},{"label":"Everyone at level 2","opts":{"groove":"hhquarters","bassFeel":"halves","compRhythm":"strumQuarters","push":false}},{"label":"Everyone at level 3","opts":{"groove":"hheighths","bassFeel":"roots","compRhythm":"strumEights","push":false}},{"label":"Everyone at level 4","opts":{"groove":"rock","bassFeel":"eighths","compRhythm":"strumFolk"}}]'></div>

## Make it a song

A loop becomes a song when the parts change between sections.

- **Verse:** quieter. Drums at level 1 or 2, guitars at level 1.
- **Chorus:** everybody up a level. Louder.
- **Ending:** play the G one last time on "1" and let it ring.

Try verse, chorus, verse, chorus, ending. Somebody counts it in: "1, 2, 3, 4".

## For the teacher

- **Grouping.** A band of four to six covers drums, bass, one or two guitars, keys and a voice
  or melody player. Students who don't play yet can start on drums level 1, bass level 1 or the
  voice level 1 line.
- **Tempo.** 92 is a starting point. Slow the band to 70 for level 1 players. Speed it up for
  the final performance.
- **Checking progress.** For each student, note the level they can play four times through without
  stopping, in time with the band. Four times through at a level is the goal before moving up.
- **Other loops.** The same parts work over **C, G, Am, F** and the other loops in
  [Four-Chord Loops](four-chord-loops.qmd). Change the chord names and the bass notes.
